guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are somewhat more favorable to Auburn than the market, but our case is not that Tennessee has been unimpressive. Tennessee reached 400 total yards in each of its first three games and scored touchdowns on 10 of 11 red-zone possessions. We also see an offense that rates among the best at creating scoring opportunities, so Auburn may have difficulty keeping Tennessee from generating enough quality possessions.

The more interesting part is Auburn’s ability to create scoring opportunities against a Tennessee defense whose strongest work has come against the pass. That gives Auburn a path to stay competitive without needing to win consistently through the air. Still, Tennessee recorded 13 sacks through three games and allowed only two pass plays of at least 20 yards, which directly challenges Auburn’s weaker offensive dimension.

That tension explains our disagreement with the market and our decision to pass. Our model sees a plausible route for Auburn to remain within range, but the matchup does not provide enough separation to justify paying the available premium.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Auburn’s passing offense against Tennessee’s pass defense. Tennessee allowed 151 passing yards per game through three games, while limiting opponents to two completions of at least 20 yards and none of 30 or more. If Auburn cannot produce efficient passes when Tennessee forces obvious passing situations, its ability to create scoring opportunities may not translate into enough points. For us, that is the matchup most likely to decide whether Auburn can validate our model’s more favorable view.

recent_game.fact: Tennessee improved to 3-0 with a 42-9 win over Kennesaw State, rushing for 268 yards and holding Kennesaw State to three field goals and no touchdowns.
Daune Morris rushed 14 times for 116 yards and a 42-yard touchdown against Kennesaw State, recording his first career 100-yard rushing game.
Faizon Brandon completed 18 of 26 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown and added 47 rushing yards and one touchdown against Kennesaw State.
Tennessee held Kennesaw State to 102 rushing yards; Arion Carter had eight tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss, while Edwin Spillman had five tackles and a forced fumble.

opponent_notes.fact: Auburn head coach Alex Golesh previously worked under Josh Heupel as offensive coordinator and tight ends coach at UCF in 2020 and at Tennessee in 2021-22.

quarterback.fact: True freshman Faizon Brandon won Tennessee's starting quarterback job in preseason camp and was officially named the starter on Aug. 24, 2026.
Through three games, Brandon had accounted for nine touchdowns—six passing and three rushing—and had not thrown an interception in 64 attempts.
Brandon had thrown at least one touchdown in each of his first three games and had twice recorded both a passing and a rushing touchdown.

offensive_personnel.fact: Tennessee's starting offensive line in each of the two most recent games was David Sanders Jr. at left tackle, Wendell Moe Jr. at left guard, Sam Pendleton at center, Sham Umarov at right guard and Jesse Perry at right tackle.
Tennessee listed eight offensive linemen with FBS starting experience, combining for 103 starts.
Mike Matthews led Tennessee through three games with 10 receptions and 189 receiving yards and was tied for the team lead with two receiving touchdowns.
Braylon Staley had caught touchdown passes in consecutive games against Georgia Tech and Kennesaw State.
DeSean Bishop had 286 rushing yards, a 95.3-yard average and four rushing touchdowns through three games.
Bishop had scored a rushing touchdown in seven consecutive games dating to Nov. 15, 2025.
Wide receiver Radarious Jackson made his first career start against Kennesaw State.

defensive_personnel.fact: Former Auburn cornerback Kayin Lee transferred to Tennessee after making 25 starts over three seasons at Auburn; the guide states that he did not allow a touchdown in 2025.
Penn State transfer linebacker Amare Campbell led Tennessee through three games with 17 tackles, including 11 solo tackles.
Penn State transfer defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam led Tennessee with 5.5 tackles for loss and 3.0 sacks through three games.
Penn State transfer safety Dejuan Lane had a team-high three passes defended, including a 41-yard interception return for a touchdown at Georgia Tech.
Defensive end Carson Gentle made his first career start against Kennesaw State.

coaching_changes.fact: Jim Knowles was named Tennessee's defensive coordinator on Dec. 11, 2025, after serving as Penn State's defensive coordinator in 2025.
Tennessee also added co-defensive coordinator and secondary coach Anthony Poindexter, LEOs coach Andrew Jackson and cornerbacks coach Derek Jones for 2026.
All five Tennessee offensive assistants returned for 2026, including offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Joey Halzle.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Ethan Davis is out for the remainder of the 2026 season with a knee injury sustained at Georgia Tech in Week 2.
Defensive back Jadais Richard is out for the season after suffering an injury during the summer.
Linebacker Arion Carter returned against Georgia Tech after serving a one-game NCAA suspension and was described as fully healthy following offseason foot surgery.

offensive_context.fact: Through three games, Tennessee averaged 47.7 points, 510.3 total yards and 298.7 rushing yards per game.
Tennessee had exceeded 400 total yards in all three games and was 11-for-11 on red-zone possessions, scoring touchdowns on 10.
Tennessee had scored a touchdown on its opening offensive possession in all three games, with each drive lasting less than three and a half minutes.
Tennessee had outscored opponents 44-0 in the second quarter and 86-10 across the second and third quarters combined.
Tennessee had produced at least 200 rushing yards in each of its first three games and had won 30 consecutive games when reaching that mark.

defensive_context.fact: Through three games under Jim Knowles, Tennessee had 13 sacks and 24 tackles for loss.
Tennessee had allowed two offensive touchdowns on 33 opponent drives through three games.
Tennessee had not allowed a first-half touchdown through three games, and its starting defense had surrendered one touchdown.
Tennessee was allowing 151.0 passing yards per game and had surrendered only two pass plays of at least 20 yards, with none reaching 30 yards.
The longest play from scrimmage Tennessee had allowed was a 34-yard rush, while the longest completed pass against it was 26 yards.

special_teams.fact: Louisville transfer Cooper Ranvier was 3-for-3 on field goals, with a long of 43 yards, and 17-for-17 on extra points through three games.
Justin Baker blocked a punt at Georgia Tech on Sept. 12, Tennessee's first blocked punt of the season.
